findings.highlight: I guess she's hoping that I've stayed the same as I've always been
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女が望む限りは、いつも通りの俺でいようって
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that, for as long as Kazusa wants it, he will remain his usual self even after the special day. The English makes Kazusa the person hoping that Haruki has remained unchanged, deleting his deliberate decision and reversing whose mental act the narration reports.
findings.japanese:
彼女が望む限りは、いつも通りの俺でいようって。
特別な日をまたいでも、変わらない俺でいようって。
findings.todokanai: I guess she's hoping that I've stayed the same as I've always been. That I haven't changed even after that special day…

findings.highlight: she's finally opened the proverbial Heavenly Rock Cave
findings.evidenceJa: 天の岩戸が、今やっと開いてくれた
findings.explanation: The Amaterasu image is of the Heavenly Rock Door or barrier finally opening, with the opening itself as the grammatical subject. The English has Kazusa actively open a cave, muddying both the movement and the culturally recognizable image; the corresponding Coda reuse later loses it altogether.
findings.japanese:
その思いが通じたのかわからないけど…
とにかく、天の岩戸が、今やっと開いてくれた。
findings.todokanai: I have no idea how she interpreted my reply, but for now, I'm just glad she's finally opened the proverbial Heavenly Rock Cave.

findings.highlight: Rather, nothing will change if I hear her opinion. I can't let my current feelings be swayed by anything other than my own will right now.
findings.evidenceJa:
というより、聞いてどうにかなるようじゃ駄目だから。
今の俺の思いを、自分の意志以外で曲げてしまっては
絶対に駄目だから。
findings.explanation: Haruki's resolve that it would be unacceptable for what he is about to hear to change anything becomes the factual prediction that nothing will change.
findings.japanese:
というより、聞いてどうにかなるようじゃ駄目だから。
今の俺の思いを、自分の意志以外で曲げてしまっては
絶対に駄目だから。
findings.todokanai: Rather, nothing will change if I hear her opinion. I can't let my current feelings be swayed by anything other than my own will right now.

findings.highlight: I perfected my poker-face a long time ago, so there's no need to worry
findings.evidenceJa: 昔からそう見えないのは認めるけど
findings.explanation: Haruki only admits that he has never looked nervous, despite actually being nervous. The English invents a deliberately perfected poker face and an assurance that there is no need to worry, turning an observation about appearances into trained concealment.
findings.japanese: …ま、昔からそう見えないのは認めるけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, I perfected my poker-face a long time ago, so there's no need to worry.

findings.explanation: The source says 402 of 683 votes was nearly sixty percent. It is approximately 58.9 percent, so 'over 60%' reverses the explicit threshold.
findings.japanese:
全有効投票数、６８３票のうち、
実に６割近くの４０２票を獲得しての、
あまりにも箔をつけ過ぎな堂々の三連覇。
findings.todokanai: Out of all the valid votes, 683 in total, 402 went to her. With a majority of over 60%, Setsuna won spectacularly for the third time in a row, uncontested.

findings.highlight: I said I don't care about it at all. You can celebrate it yourself
findings.evidenceJa: だからあたしを祝ったってしょうがないだろ。自分で勝手に祝杯でも上げてろ
findings.explanation: Kazusa says there is no point congratulating her and tells Haruki to raise his own celebratory toast instead. The English repeats a declaration of indifference, deleting the self-effacing redirection of the celebration and making her more dismissive.
findings.japanese:
「だからあたしを祝ったってしょうがないだろ。
自分で勝手に祝杯でも上げてろ…」
findings.todokanai: "I said I don't care about it at all. You can celebrate it yourself…"

findings.highlight: Touma came into my view before I knew it
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬は、いつの間にか視界に納めてた
findings.explanation: The object carried over from the preceding line is Haruki's nod: Kazusa had brought it into her field of vision and was watching him. The English reverses the perceiver and says Kazusa entered Haruki's view.
findings.japanese: 冬馬は、いつの間にか視界に納めてた。
findings.todokanai: Touma came into my view before I knew it.

findings.evidenceJa: でも、とうとう来てしまったって気持ちばかりだ。
findings.explanation: Haruki feels that the long-awaited moment has finally arrived; the English says only that Kazusa finally said it.
findings.japanese: でも、とうとう来てしまったって気持ちばかりだ。

findings.highlight: Your two friends would be leaving you out, spending more time with each other
findings.evidenceJa: 二人の友達を、片方だけひいきしたみたいで
findings.explanation: Haruki worries that inviting Setsuna alone would make it look as though he were favoring one of his two friends. The English instead makes the two friends exclude Kazusa by spending time with each other, reversing who performs the socially questionable action.
findings.japanese: 「…二人の友達を、片方だけひいきしたみたいで」
findings.todokanai: "…Your two friends would be leaving you out, spending more time with each other…"

findings.highlight: All that means nothing to me
findings.explanation: Kazusa answers Haruki's proposed reason for separating their friendships by saying there is no such reason, then reminds him she has said so before. 'All that means nothing to me' turns her acceptance of continued association into emotional dismissal.
findings.japanese:
「そんなの、なにもない。
だって、前にも言っただろ？」
findings.todokanai: "All that means nothing to me. I told you before, didn't I?"

findings.highlight: From now on, our bonds will deepen and become stronger, without a doubt.
findings.evidenceJa:
これから絆を深く、
そして強くしていかなくちゃならないんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki frames strengthening the bond among the three as an obligation; the English predicts that the friendship will naturally grow.
findings.japanese:
これから絆を深く、
そして強くしていかなくちゃならないんだから。
findings.todokanai: From now on, our bonds will deepen and become stronger, without a doubt.
